subject.title: [Bug]: Gateway auth token dropped from service-env on update (recurs despite 2026.7.1 fix) + CLI can't auth locally

question: Should local interactive CLI commands automatically obtain credentials from the managed local-gateway SecretRef path, or should OpenClaw retain explicit token/password input and only repair the service-env preservation regression?
rationale: Repairing the service update path is a compatibility bug, but making a service-only credential transparently available to interactive commands changes the credential-access boundary and is not settled by the current documented explicit-input behavior.

options.title: Repair service preservation only
options.body: Preserve the existing managed value for configured SecretRefs across update/reinstall and retain explicit CLI credential sources as the supported interactive contract.

options.title: Add a scoped local CLI resolver
options.body: Define and document a restricted local-mode resolver that can authenticate CLI commands without exporting the managed gateway token into the user shell.

recommendation.title: Repair service preservation only
recommendation.body: Preserve the existing managed value for configured SecretRefs across update/reinstall and retain explicit CLI credential sources as the supported interactive contract.

likelyOwner.reason: The released managed service-env SecretRef work is the closest proven ownership signal for both the regression boundary and a compatible repair.
